question: GQ-001
subject: I killed a 45-minute build by reading the database it was writing — twice
what_happened: testing the search CLI against the live corpus during a rebuild took read locks at a commit point; the modern-index build died with "database is locked (5)" after 1,394,000 of 4,130,649 rows. The retry died the same way.
the_underlying_fragility: NOT ONE script in the pipeline had a busy timeout — build-external-passages, migrate-book-external, build-library-page, corpus-integrity and add-longs-variants all failed instantly on any lock contention
why_that_matters_beyond_my_mistake: a corpus that cannot be READ while it rebuilds has ~45 minutes of downtime per ingest cycle, and the rebuild is the long-running side — so it is the side that must wait

the_fix.writers: .timeout 60000 — a writer would have to redo 45 minutes
the_fix.verified: ran a reader DURING a write: reader exit 0, writer still alive

the_guard_i_already_had_did_not_cover_th: refuse_if_ingesting blocks a rebuild while an INGEST runs; it says nothing about readers, and readers were the problem
